newsitem.title: UK: British food poisoning death toll now 15.
newsitem.headline: British food poisoning death toll now 15.

text.p: Fifteen people have now died in Britain's worst outbreak of food poisoning, officials said on Thursday.
A 76-year-old man and a 78-year-old woman died on Wednesday evening in hospital in the Scottish town of Airdrie, local health board officials said.
All those who have died in one of the most serious outbreaks of food poisoning ever recorded in the world have been elderly.
Most of the cases, in which victims contract the E coli strain of food poisoning, are linked to two Scottish butcher's shops -- one of which recently won awards for its products.
More than 300 people have reported symptoms of the poisoning, which can cause kidney failure in the vulnerable.
A spokesman also said that 178 people in the area were suffering from E coli, an increase of 15 on Wednesday.
E coli is a bacteria normally found in the guts of cattle, sheep and people. It is usually harmless but one strain, known as 0157, can cause brain damage and kidney failure.
It gets into food via improper slaughtering techniques or through manure used as fertiliser.
The deadliest outbreak of E coli was in Canada, where 19 old people infected in a nursing home died in September 1985.
Eleven people, mostly schoolchildren, died in an outbreak in Japan in July and 9,500 became ill.
